basis: Cataracts/glaucoma, congenital septal heart defects and tethered spinal cord define the syndrome; joint limitation lacks a clear frequency.
Familial liver cirrhosis; unspecified antigenemia alone does not establish an infectious or immune mechanism.
Paget carcinoma involves the squamous epithelium of the anal canal; cutaneous extension is not established.
Inherited podocyte disease causing glomerulosclerosis and nephrotic syndrome; no established extrarenal damage.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction defines PCD; chronic middle-ear inflammation affects 30-79%. Laterality defects alone do not establish cardiac damage.
Carcinoma originates in the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, which belong to the pulmonary axis.
Tick-borne viral CNS infection; encephalitis defines this concept despite the low neurologic attack rate among all infected people. Cytopenias are transient.
Neurological syndrome caused by deficient CNS folate transport or turnover; folate metabolism outside the nervous system is normal.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no organ axis.
Hereditary toe malformation with an annotated skeletal abnormality.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder. Cerebral visual impairment in 2/6 is CNS dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Congenital spinal cord and meningeal dysraphism with a fibroneural or spinal cord stalk; additional skeletal damage is not established.
Developmental disability and axonal neuropathy define DIGFAN; pigmentary retinopathy in 5/6 and hearing impairment in 11/19 support eye and ear involvement.
Integumentary malignancy supports the skin axis; breast and Bartholin gland subtypes have no anatomical axis, and lymphoma is not universal.
Congenital cleft lip and palate affect oral structures, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Neoplasm originates in the floor of the mouth.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; a neurological ancestor does not establish damage outside the eye.
Mitochondrial myopathy defines progressive ophthalmoplegia; parkinsonism in 2/2 and sensory neuropathy in 1/2 support neurologic involvement, though samples are small.
Red-cell membrane disease causes spherocytosis and hemolysis. Splenomegaly is within the blood axis; jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Skeletal overgrowth, fragile hyperelastic skin and cerebral white-matter lesions define the syndrome; proptosis alone does not establish eye damage.
Benign tumor occupies the retina; retinal location takes precedence over broad nervous-system ancestry.
Galactose metabolic disease with defining neonatal liver injury; neurologic abnormalities occur in 80-99%, cataracts in 30-79%. Coagulopathy is secondary to liver failure.
Viral or bacterial infection directly involves the external, middle or inner ear.
Tuberculosis directly infects the epididymis. Reproductive anatomy has no axis; urinary tract involvement is not established.
Neoplasms of connective tissue, skeletal structures and soft tissue belong to the musculoskeletal axis; no additional site applies across the group.
